note.explanation: Enthalpy (H) is the total heat content of a system. We cannot measure H directly, but we can measure how much it changes, ΔH. Heat is energy being transferred from a hotter body to a colder body. At constant pressure, a system’s enthalpy change equals the heat it absorbs or releases.
examples: For 2 CO(g) + O₂(g) → 2 CO₂(g), ΔH° = -566.0 kJ. The negative value means heat is released.
If a system absorbs heat at constant pressure, its enthalpy increases.
note.checkAnswer: The total enthalpy H cannot be measured directly; the enthalpy change ΔH can be measured.
note.simple: Enthalpy is the energy content of a system. Heat is energy moving between bodies. We measure a change in enthalpy, not the system’s total enthalpy.

explain.title: Enthalpy and its symbols
explain.body: “The total amount of heat energy present in a molecule under standard conditions (0°C temperature and 760 mm pressure) is also called its heat content. Enthalpy is the measurement of energy in a thermodynamic system. The quantity of enthalpy is equal to the total heat content of a system. Enthalpy of a system is represented by (H) while the change in enthalpy which a system undergoes is represented by ΔH.” In questions, keep H and ΔH distinct.

explain.title: What can be measured?
explain.body: “The total enthalpy (H) of a system cannot be measured directly. However, the change in enthalpy ΔH brought about in a system can be measured comparatively easily.” So chemistry questions usually compare the energy before and after a change.

explain.title: Standard enthalpy of reaction
explain.body: “In Chemistry, the standard enthalpy of reaction (ΔH°) is the enthalpy change when reactants in their standard states undergo reaction to produce products in their standard states.” It is also called the standard enthalpy change or heat of reaction at constant pressure.

explain.title: Heat compared with enthalpy
explain.body: “Heat is a form of energy that flows from hot body to a cold body because of a difference in temperature.” Enthalpy is part of a system and depends on its molecules, composition and structure. At constant pressure, enthalpy change equals the heat evolved or absorbed.

mistakes: Do not use H and ΔH as if they mean the same thing: H is enthalpy, while ΔH is its change.
Do not describe heat as energy stored in the system; heat is energy being transferred.
Do not say a negative ΔH means heat is absorbed. Negative ΔH means heat is released to the surroundings.
When defining standard enthalpy of reaction, do not leave out that reactants and products are in their standard states.
Do not forget to state the constant-pressure condition when giving the equality between enthalpy change and heat.
